candidates.name: Glioma
support_spans: Vitreous biopsy: Hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm, small to medium-sized cells with scant cytoplasm and oval, pleomorphic, hyperchromatic nuclei
Immunohistochemistry: Positive for glial fibrillary acid protein, oligodendrocyte transcription factor 2, mutant IDH-1 protein, p53; Loss of ATRX protein; Ki-67 proliferation index ~10%
candidates.why: The presence of astrocytic neoplasm and specific immunohistochemical markers in the vitreous biopsy suggests a glioma.

candidates.name: Optic Nerve Glioma
support_spans: Right eye showed full visual field, right-sided relative afferent pupillary defect, unremarkable anterior segment, and mild swelling of the optic disc
MRI at Onset of Vision Loss: Focal enhancement along enlarged right optic nerve
candidates.why: The initial presentation of optic disc swelling and subsequent imaging findings of an enlarged optic nerve with enhancement suggest an optic nerve glioma.

candidates.name: Idiopathic Optic Neuritis
support_spans: Right eye showed full visual field, right-sided relative afferent pupillary defect, unremarkable anterior segment, and mild swelling of the optic disc
contradict_spans: Vitreous biopsy: Hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm
candidates.why: The initial presentation of optic disc swelling and a relative afferent pupillary defect could suggest idiopathic optic neuritis, but the subsequent biopsy results indicate a neoplastic process.

candidates.name: Optic Nerve Glioma
support_spans: Focal enhancement along enlarged right optic nerve
Diffuse enlargement of orbital portion of right optic nerve, enhancement of nerve sheath
candidates.why: The patient's presentation with sudden vision loss and optic disc swelling, combined with imaging findings of an enlarged optic nerve and enhancement of the nerve sheath, suggests an optic nerve glioma.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may be easily missed due to its rarity and the patient's complex treatment regimen, which includes immunotherapy and systemic steroids.

candidates.name: Retinal Artery Occlusion
support_spans: Occlusion of the superior branch artery
Combined occlusion of the central retinal artery and vein
candidates.why: The patient's sudden vision loss and findings of retinal artery occlusion on examination and imaging suggest a retinal artery occlusion.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may be overlooked due to the patient's underlying treatment with bevacizumab, which can increase the risk of thrombotic events.
